title: A/B inspection & regression triage — 1:1 prep
content:
Context:
Quick prep notes for 1:1 with Maya / Luis — follow-up from last weekly Optimize review. We saw a noticeable quality drop on the customer-facing prompt set after rolling prompt_v3 as variant in the A/B. Need to triage, capture immediate mitigations, and agree on next steps.

Meeting objective:
- Align on whether this is a prompt regression vs. data shift vs. post-quantization issue.
- Triage high-priority prompt examples and decide rollback/mitigation plan.
- Assign owners for reproducibility checks, deeper evals, and monitoring updates.

Quick TL;DR (what I saw):
- A/B run (eval-run:2026-04-25-7b9f) comparing control (prompt_v2) vs variant (prompt_v3).
- Primary signal: mean helpfulness score dropped from ~0.78 -> 0.69 on release-customer-set (n=1,200).
- Secondary signal: safety alert rate +1.8% absolute on the same set (mostly off-topic hallucination flags).
- Latency and cost: p50/p95 latency ~unchanged; token count slightly higher (+3%), likely due to longer completed outputs.
- Initial hypothesis: prompt_v3 increases verbosity which worsens hallucination surface area for a subset of queries. Could also be interaction with quantized model path (int8) for long-form outputs.

Repro steps (lightweight) — run before 1:1 if possible:
1) Pull the eval run: ./tools/eval_cli download --run-id 2026-04-25-7b9f --out ./tmp/eval-7b9f
2) Quick diff summary: python tools/eval_diff.py --a ./tmp/eval-7b9f/control --b ./tmp/eval-7b9f/variant --metrics helpfulness safety ngram-overlap
3) Spot-check examples: head -n 50 tmp/eval-7b9f/variant/failing_examples.csv | sed -n '1,50p'
4) Re-run 100 seeded queries locally with model pinned to float16 (no quant) to test quantization interaction: python tools/local_eval.py --seed 42 --count 100 --prompt-set release-customer-set --model rwd-open-1-7b --quant none

Open questions to ask in the meeting:
- Did the rollout use the same model binary/quantization profile as control? (If not, we probably have a confound.)
- Which subset of prompts drives the drop? (single-turn vs multi-turn; instruction-heavy vs slot-filling)
- Any recent downstream reranker changes? Could evaluation pipeline normalization change scores?
- Are the safety flags real (model behavior) or classifier sensitivity drift?

Priority actions (short-term mitigation) — propose in 1:1:
- Rollback plan: temporary revert to prompt_v2 for the 10% of traffic that uses release-customer-set prompts. Owner: Maya. Due: 2026-04-29.
- Hotfix prompts: Prepare a conservative prompt_v3a that reduces verbosity (trim instructions + cap generation at 150 tokens). Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-04-28 (prototype).
- Monitoring alert: add a per-prompt-set helpfulness delta alert (threshold: -0.05 absolute). Owner: Rajiv. Due: 2026-05-01.

Investigation actions (owners + notes):
- Repro + quant check (Luis): run the float16 vs int8 comparison across failing subset (n=500). Command + dataset in linked_artifacts. Due: 2026-04-30.
- Prompt-level clustering (Sofia): cluster failing prompts by intent/length to identify patterns. Use k=8, silhouette >= 0.22 to guide clusters. Due: 2026-04-30.
- Reranker / postproc audit (Maya): verify no scoring normalization changed in pipeline between control and variant runs. Check PRs in last two weeks. Due: 2026-04-29.
- Safety classifier drift check (DataOps): compare classifier thresholds/stats between 2026-04-01..2026-04-25. Tagging DataOps slack/channel. Due: 2026-05-03.

Metrics to bring to meeting (quick numbers I will share):
- Helpful score: control 0.783 -> variant 0.693 (±0.02, bootstrap CI)
- Safety flag rate: control 3.4% -> variant 5.2%
- Avg token count: control 42.1 -> variant 43.4
- N overall eval samples: 1,198
- Top 5 failing examples attached in eval artifact (linked above).

Notes-to-self / conversation bullets:
- If rollback harms any specific enterprise test (billing etc), propose 1:1 traffic slicing to only rollback the release-customer-set wave.
- Emphasize reproducibility: always pin model binary + quant profile in eval artifact metadata.
- Check whether Optimize's automatic batching changed input truncation or padding that could have influenced outputs.

Follow-up structure (how we'll track):
- I will create a Jira OPT-XXXX (triage ticket) that cross-links the eval run, the PRs, and the rollback plan. Add owners above as assignees.
- Weekly checkpoint: quick results summary in Optimize weekly sync (Friday). If rollout rollback happens, mark as incident and write 1-page postmortem within 7 days.

Misc scratch ideas (low-effort experiments):
- Soft prompt shim: add short guard token at start of prompts that nudges concision ("TL;DR: concise answer, prefer bullet list"). A/B this on 5% traffic. Low risk.
- Prompt templating: canonicalize instruction phrasing across variant/control to isolate wording changes.

Immediate prep for 1:1 (what I'll ask them):
- Maya: confirm rollback authority and any customer impact constraints.
- Luis: confirm time to run quant vs float smoke tests and whether we have GPU capacity for a 500-run sweep today.
- Rajiv: confirm alerting pipeline and whether we can trigger an inbox notification for product ops on threshold breach.

End notes / reminders:
- Bring the 10 worst examples (with model outputs) into the call for quick screen-sharing.
- Save the eval-run artifact in S3 under /optimize/tmp for redundancy before any destructive steps.

-- Sofia
